title: Operations Management Adventure 2: Lean & Quality
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Kaizen, JIT, TQM and Six Sigma — the lean and quality toolkit.
meta_desc: Business Management Ops: lean (Kaizen, JIT) and quality management (TQM, Six Sigma).
final_note: You learned lean production tools and the two main quality management systems.

concepts.def: Workers meet to solve quality issues

walkthroughs.body_html:
Lean came from the Toyota Production System.

Lean attacks the seven muda (wastes): transport, inventory, motion, waiting, overproduction, over-processing, defects.

Tools include Kaizen, JIT, 5S, kanban and andon cords.

Kaizen means 'change for the better' — many small workforce-led improvements rather than top-down upheaval.

Just-in-time aligns stock arrival to production. Less stock means lower storage cost but high vulnerability — one supplier delay halts the line.

TQM (Deming) embeds quality across every department: 'right first time'.

Six Sigma (Motorola, 1986) uses statistics to reach 3.4 defects per million opportunities through DMAIC: Define, Measure, Analyse, Improve, Control.

Why might a business adopt corporate social responsibility (CSR)?
options: CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
Reasons include genuine ethics, but also commercial benefits — improved reputation, customer loyalty, employee retention, and reduced regulatory or reputational risk.
CSR is purely about being ethical with no business benefit.
Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a mission statement?
options: CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
A mission statement is a description of what products the business sells.
A mission statement is a list of financial targets.
To define the business's core purpose and values, guiding decisions and communicating identity to stakeholders — answering 'why we exist'.

mcqs.q: Which sector does manufacturing belong to?
options: The secondary sector — which transforms raw materials from the primary sector (farming, mining) into finished goods.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
Manufacturing is in the primary sector because it makes things.
